topic: Theory: Dragon's Mary Geoise raid and eight-nation revolution (chapter 1083) were built to squeeze the Holy Land and pull the Knights of God away from it, which fits the Elbaph arc
title: Dragon Baited The Knights Of God Out Of Mary Geoise
description:
Chapter 1083 shows Dragon saying Sabo's Mary Geoise raid held Marine eyes while twelve nations rose up and the Heavenly Tribute dried up. This theory follows that plan to the Knights of God now stuck in Elbaph, and to the unexplained fire at the Holy Land.

We steelman the objection that Dragon never planned Elbaph, weigh the Blackbeard and Red Hair suspects, and show why a squeezed Imu fits Dragon's patience from Loguetown onward. Do you think the Revolutionary Army burned Mary Geoise, or someone else?

comment: Who burned Mary Geoise: the Revolutionary Army following Dragon's plan, or Blackbeard going after the same prize?

lines.text: Everyone remembers Sabo's raid on Mary Geoise as a rescue mission.

lines.text: Free Kuma, free the slaves, break the Celestial Dragons' symbol. Then chapter 1083 hands us a second job.

shot.fallback: revolutionaries leading chained people out of a holy city

lines.text: Did Monkey D. Dragon quietly bait the Knights of God out of Mary Geoise, long before anyone saw them in Elbaph?

shot.fallback: hooded revolutionary leader looking over a world map

lines.text: I know how that sounds. Dragon barely appears on the page, and he never swings at anyone.

shot.fallback: hooded man standing in a storm on a rooftop

lines.text: But his plan only needs two things. A very loud operation, and a very quiet one.

shot.fallback: three revolutionaries talking in a dim command room

lines.text: The loud one made headlines in every newspaper on the Grand Line.

shot.search: Sabo Flame Emperor newspaper Mary Geoise
shot.fallback: newspaper headline about a masked revolutionary

lines.text: The quiet one is why Mary Geoise went hungry, and why its guards started to feel stretched.

shot.search: Mary Geoise Holy Land Celestial Dragons
shot.fallback: white holy city under a grey sky

lines.text: And if I'm right, one of the biggest Knights of God moves in the whole Elbaph arc started in this chapter.

shot.search: Knights of God Elbaph Imu Gunko
shot.fallback: armored holy knights marching across a giant forest

lines.text: So let's follow Dragon's logic, one piece at a time, and see where it lands us...

shot.search: Dragon Monkey D. Dragon Revolutionary Army
shot.fallback: revolutionary commander silhouette before dawn

lines.text: The loud operation first.

shot.search: Sabo Mary Geoise raid Revolutionary Army
shot.fallback: masked revolutionary sneaking into a holy city

lines.text: Sabo, Karasu, Morley and Lindbergh walk into the one place on Earth nobody is supposed to attack.

shot.search: Sabo Karasu Morley Lindbergh Mary Geoise
shot.fallback: four revolutionary commanders approaching a palace gate

lines.text: In chapter 1083, Sabo reports back to Dragon and Ivankov, and he lists exactly three things they pulled off.

shot.fallback: masked young man reporting to two leaders

lines.text: One, they declared war by destroying the World Nobles' symbol, right in their own front yard.

shot.search: Sabo destroys Celestial Dragons symbol Mary Geoise
shot.fallback: revolutionary smashing a golden emblem

lines.text: Two, they freed Kuma from the Celestial Dragons, along with as many slaves as they could reach.

shot.fallback: slaves walking free from a courtyard

lines.text: Three, they destroyed the Holy Land's food reserves. And that third goal is the one I want you to hold onto.

shot.search: Sabo Mary Geoise food reserves destroyed
shot.fallback: burning storehouse in a white city

lines.text: Because nobody breaks into the world's richest city to burn the pantry unless the plan is about hunger.

shot.search: Mary Geoise Celestial Dragons banquet food
shot.fallback: nobles eating at a huge table in a palace

lines.text: Meanwhile, Karasu and Morley hold off Admiral Fujitora and Ryokugyu so the others can finish the job.

shot.search: Karasu Morley Fujitora Ryokugyu Mary Geoise
shot.fallback: two revolutionaries facing two admirals

lines.text: Lindbergh frees the slaves while they hold the line, and Sabo hunts for the keys to the collars and chains.

shot.search: Lindbergh Sabo slaves freed keys Mary Geoise
shot.fallback: big revolutionary breaking chains in a courtyard

lines.text: Two admirals, in the Holy Land, and the Revolutionary Army still walks out. That alone is a statement.

shot.fallback: two admirals standing in front of a palace

lines.text: That matters for the theory, because it proves the Holy Land can be reached. Once is a fluke, and twice is a plan.

shot.search: Mary Geoise Red Line Sabo Karasu
shot.fallback: revolutionaries standing on the edge of a giant red wall

lines.text: Now here's the line most people skim past. Dragon tells Sabo the raid kept most Marine eyes locked on him.

shot.search: Dragon tells Sabo Marines attention chapter 1083
shot.fallback: leader speaking calmly to a masked young man

lines.text: Read that again. He isn't only praising a rescue. He's describing Sabo as the noise that covered something else.

shot.fallback: revolutionary leader pointing at a map

lines.text: Think about what a decoy needs. It has to be impressive enough that nobody asks what else is happening.

shot.search: Sabo Mary Geoise flag destroyed Celestial Dragon
shot.fallback: revolutionary standing on a ruined golden flag

lines.text: A masked man tearing down the World Nobles' symbol is exactly that. The whole world looked up at the Holy Land.

shot.search: Sabo Flame Emperor masked Mary Geoise
shot.fallback: masked man raising a flame in a white city

lines.text: And Sabo may not even know how loud he was being on purpose.

shot.search: Sabo Flame Emperor Revolutionary Army Chief of Staff
shot.fallback: masked man looking at a newspaper

lines.text: I think that's very Dragon. We've seen the move before, all the way back in chapter 100.

shot.fallback: hooded man arriving in a storm over a town

lines.text: At Loguetown, Smoker has Luffy cornered and the whole port is watching him.

shot.fallback: white haired marine with two jittes facing a boy

lines.text: Then Dragon arrives, a storm tears through the town, and everyone is hurled away from Luffy.

shot.fallback: strong wind scattering marines in a harbor town

lines.text: The storm took every eye in town, and Luffy walked out.

shot.search: Dragon Loguetown Luffy escape Going Merry
shot.fallback: boy running to a small ship through a storm

lines.text: The Marines, the Government and even Luffy were all watching the wrong thing, and the right thing walked away.

shot.fallback: marines and a boy staring at a storm

lines.text: Same method, different scale. Make the noise somewhere else, and move your real piece through the gap.

shot.fallback: two figures splitting paths on a map

lines.text: So if the Mary Geoise raid was the noise, what exactly was it covering?

shot.fallback: leader looking at a map with twelve red marks

lines.text: This is where the story gets quiet, and where I think the real revolution lives...

shot.search: Revolutionary Army world map nations uprising
shot.fallback: map of countries with burning marks

lines.text: Chapter 1083 says the Revolutionary Army's influence set off uprisings in twelve nations.

shot.fallback: crowds raising banners in twelve small kingdoms

lines.text: Eight of them held. That is the Eight-Nation Revolution, and it is one of the least discussed events in the series.

shot.fallback: eight flags rising over small kingdoms

lines.text: And the reason people stopped talking about it is simple. Most of it only arrives as dialogue.

shot.fallback: crowd cheering outside a palace

lines.text: Fans quote the number, twelve and eight, and move on. I think the number is the least interesting part.

shot.fallback: newspaper headline about a rebellion

lines.text: No big fight, no panel of Dragon holding a banner. Just a list of countries that stopped obeying.

shot.fallback: leader in a hood overlooking a city

lines.text: What did they stop doing? Paying the Heavenly Tribute to the World Nobles, and shipping their resources upward.

shot.fallback: ships loaded with gold heading to a holy city

lines.text: The Celestial Dragons do not farm, mine or build anything. Everything they own comes up the Red Line from somewhere else.

shot.search: Celestial Dragons Mary Geoise Red Line tribute
shot.fallback: golden palaces on top of a huge red wall

lines.text: When twelve countries stop paying, the Holy Land loses more than gold. It loses the food and luxury it was built on.

shot.search: Celestial Dragons Mary Geoise luxury slaves
shot.fallback: nobles lounging beside bowing servants

lines.text: Dragon says the Revolutionary Army is also hitting World Government supply carriers, all over the world.

shot.search: Revolutionary Army supply carriers attack ships
shot.fallback: revolutionaries boarding a cargo ship at sea

lines.text: That means the Revolutionary Army is fighting a logistics war, which is the least glamorous kind and the hardest to stop.

shot.search: Revolutionary Army logistics war supply ships
shot.fallback: stacked crates on a dock at night

lines.text: He admits they aren't cutting everything off. But he's very clear that they are squeezing.

shot.fallback: leader pressing a fist into an open palm

lines.text: Put the pieces together and the Mary Geoise raid starts to look like a stress test.

shot.search: Sabo Mary Geoise Revolutionary Army Kuma
shot.fallback: nobles panicking inside a palace

lines.text: Burn the food reserves, block the tribute, hit the carriers. The Holy Land has less supply and less safety, all at once.

shot.search: Mary Geoise Holy Land food reserves burning
shot.fallback: burning storehouse in a white city

lines.text: That's what I mean by a quiet operation. It doesn't win a battle. It just makes the other side more expensive to run.

shot.fallback: leader studying a map by candlelight

lines.text: And you can see the cost on the Celestial Dragons' side almost immediately.

shot.fallback: five elders sitting in a dark chamber

lines.text: Because of what happens to Lulusia, one of the kingdoms that rebelled.

shot.fallback: small kingdom with rebels cheering a masked visitor

lines.text: By the time Dragon gives his report, Lulusia is already gone from the map.

shot.fallback: glowing weapon firing at a distant island

lines.text: The wiki says Imu and the Five Elders used an Ancient Weapon on it as a Mother Flame test.

shot.search: Lulusia Mother Flame Ancient Weapon Imu
shot.fallback: dark figure approving a ritual in a throne room

lines.text: The Five Elders were part of that decision. A wiped-out rebel kingdom scares everyone else into staying quiet.

shot.fallback: five old men seated around a table

lines.text: Think about what that tells us. The throne room answers a rebellion with a demonstration, not a discussion.

shot.fallback: dark chair with a shadow looming over it

lines.text: That also tells us something about the fear underneath. If Imu were calm, nobody would need a weapon to make a point.

shot.search: Imu Mary Geoise throne shadow fear
shot.fallback: shadowed throne with a dark figure

lines.text: So Dragon isn't only starving Mary Geoise. He's testing how Imu reacts when it gets squeezed.

shot.fallback: revolutionary leader looking at a distant palace

lines.text: And the answer, so far, is that Imu reacts hard, early, and with tools that cost something to use.

shot.fallback: glowing ancient weapon over a sea

lines.text: Which brings me to the sentence in chapter 1083 I keep coming back to. Dragon names the Knights of God...

shot.search: Dragon Knights of God chapter 1083 prediction
shot.fallback: leader speaking in a dim room about armored knights

lines.text: Dragon says the World Government will not accept this situation.

shot.search: Dragon World Government Revolutionary Army Ivankov
shot.fallback: leader speaking seriously to a friend

lines.text: He expects them to send the Knights of God, and he calls that the real battle.

shot.search: Dragon Knights of God real battle
shot.fallback: armored figures under a pale light

lines.text: Notice what he does not say. He doesn't say we win that fight. He says that's when it really starts.

shot.fallback: three revolutionaries around a table

lines.text: He also doesn't order the army to stand ready at the gates. He lets the Government move first, and then reads the response.

shot.search: Dragon Revolutionary Army waits Government move
shot.fallback: leader watching a harbor from a cliff

lines.text: To me that is the clearest sign this is a trap built out of patience, not a charge built out of rage.

shot.search: Dragon Ivankov Sabo trap patience plan
shot.fallback: three revolutionaries around a map with markers

lines.text: That's a general talking about timing. He knows the Knights are coming, and he knows what they cost.

shot.fallback: leader at a map table with markers

lines.text: The Knights of God are an elite group of Celestial Dragons, and they enforce the Holy Land's order.

shot.search: Knights of God Celestial Dragons Imu enforcers
shot.fallback: group of armored nobles in a dark hall

lines.text: When they move, it's because the usual Marines and Cipher Pol agents weren't enough. That's a loud admission.

shot.search: Knights of God Marines Cipher Pol Mary Geoise
shot.fallback: marines saluting before dark armored figures

lines.text: So where do the Knights of God actually go once the pressure builds up?

shot.search: Knights of God Elbaph arc Sommers Gunko
shot.fallback: armored knights arriving on a giant island

lines.text: They go where Imu sends them, and this time Imu sent them far from the Holy Land.

shot.search: Knights of God Holy Land Mary Geoise guards
shot.fallback: armored knights standing guard in a white hall

lines.text: Elbaph. The land of the giants, and the home of Harald's legacy, a place the Holy Land clearly wants badly.

shot.fallback: huge giant village with wooden towers

lines.text: Gunko leads the Knights there, with Shepherd Sommers and Rimoshifu Killingham at his side.

shot.search: Gunko Shamrock Sommers Elbaph Knights of God
shot.fallback: four armored nobles gathering on a giant island

lines.text: Sommers and Killingham are not small names, and both use Devil Fruit powers in this operation.

shot.search: Sommers Ito Ito no Mi thorny vines
shot.fallback: smiling knight with thorny vines around him

lines.text: In the operation, they kidnap Elbaph's schoolchildren and use them to force the elder Jarul to let the Owl Library burn.

shot.fallback: giant children locked in a cage near a library

lines.text: Look at how that plan works. A small group of Knights, deep in giant territory, using hostages instead of armies.

shot.search: Knights of God Elbaph children hostages plan
shot.fallback: small group of knights standing over a giant village

lines.text: Hostages, a library, a school. It is cruel, and it is a plan for a force that cannot afford losses.

shot.search: Elbaph Walrus Academy library children Knights
shot.fallback: giant school building with a worried crowd

lines.text: You do not play it that way when your home base has hundreds of armed guards ready to go.

shot.fallback: rows of palace guards in white uniforms

lines.text: You play it that way when your home base is short on people, short on supplies, and short on patience.

shot.search: Mary Geoise Holy Land under pressure
shot.fallback: burning white city skyline

lines.text: And that is the moment in the story where the Holy Land itself catches fire.

shot.search: Mary Geoise attack fire burning Holy Land
shot.fallback: smoke rising from a white palace city

lines.text: While the Knights are busy in Elbaph, an unknown force hits Mary Geoise, and much of it burns.

shot.search: Mary Geoise burning unknown attackers Elbaph
shot.fallback: palace city engulfed in smoke at night

lines.text: Shamrock returns to Mary Geoise, and only then is the situation stabilized, though much of the Holy Land stays in ruins.

shot.fallback: tall knight walking through ruined white streets

lines.text: Nobody has told us who the attackers were. Not in the chapters I've read, and not in anything I can verify.

shot.fallback: mystery silhouettes watching a burning palace

lines.text: So I won't tell you Dragon burned Mary Geoise. I don't know that, and neither does anyone else.

shot.fallback: revolutionary leader looking at a palace city from afar

lines.text: But I will tell you the Revolutionary Army has already broken into the Holy Land once...

shot.search: Sabo Karasu Morley Lindbergh Mary Geoise raid
shot.fallback: four masked commanders on rooftop above a holy city

lines.text: Now the strongest counter-argument, because this theory has a real hole in it.

shot.search: Elbaph arc giants Luffy Loki Imu
shot.fallback: giant forest with a dark sky

lines.text: Elbaph isn't Dragon's war. The Knights went there for Elbaph's own reasons, and Imu went there for his.

shot.fallback: girl with glowing eyes standing over a giant village

lines.text: Imu possessed Gunko to push the operation along, and the Knights' real goal is tied to the giants, not to the Revolutionary Army.

shot.fallback: girl with glowing red eyes

lines.text: And honestly, I think that's mostly right. Dragon did not send the Knights of God to Elbaph.

shot.fallback: hooded leader far from a giant island

lines.text: Dragon doesn't control Elbaph, Harald's legacy, or whatever Imu is hunting in the giants' library.

shot.fallback: old giant king and ancient books

lines.text: So the theory can't be that Dragon planned Elbaph. It has to be smaller, and more believable than that.

shot.fallback: leader tracing a route on a map

lines.text: Here's my read. Dragon didn't choose where the Knights would go. He chose what Mary Geoise would look like when they left.

shot.search: Dragon Mary Geoise Knights of God leave
shot.fallback: empty white palace corridor at dusk

lines.text: A government that is hungry, short on tribute, and scared of another raid has fewer ways to protect its home.

shot.fallback: nobles whispering in a white hallway

lines.text: Fear makes governments sloppy. A sloppy throne is exactly where a patient enemy waits.

shot.search: Celestial Dragons fear Mary Geoise panic
shot.fallback: nobles fleeing through marble halls

lines.text: The Knights are Imu's best tool, and every Knight deployed in Elbaph is a Knight not standing at the Holy Land's gates.

shot.search: Knights of God deployed Elbaph Mary Geoise gates
shot.fallback: armored knight leaving a palace gate

lines.text: That's a trade. And the Revolutionary Army spent time making sure that trade hurts.

shot.fallback: leader and army gathering on a hill

lines.text: Every revolution Dragon sparked pulled a little more attention, a little more money and a few more soldiers away from the center.

shot.fallback: map with red circles around small kingdoms

lines.text: Now, the other objection. Some fans think the fire at Mary Geoise could be the Blackbeard Pirates, or even the Red Hair Pirates.

shot.search: Blackbeard Pirates Red Hair Pirates Mary Geoise
shot.fallback: two pirate flags over a dark sea

lines.text: That's possible. Nothing in the text rules it out, and I'm not going to pretend it does.

shot.fallback: big grinning pirate holding a mug

lines.text: But think about who gets hurt by a burning Holy Land. The throne, the nobles, and the Knights' home.

shot.search: Mary Geoise nobles throne room burning
shot.fallback: nobles running through a smoky palace

lines.text: The Revolutionary Army has the motive, the history, and a stated goal of doing exactly this kind of damage.

shot.search: Revolutionary Army Sabo Mary Geoise motive
shot.fallback: revolutionaries on a rooftop above a holy city

lines.text: The Blackbeard Pirates have a motive too, but their goal has always been the strongest fruits and the world's biggest prize.

shot.fallback: dark pirate crew on a ship at night

lines.text: I'm not saying the Revolutionary Army did it. I'm saying only one side has already told us how it would.

shot.fallback: two leaders looking at a palace sketch

lines.text: Which leaves one detail about Dragon himself that I think fans have been underrating...

shot.fallback: hooded figure in a long dark coat

lines.text: Dragon has never needed to be the loudest person in the room.

shot.search: Dragon Monkey D. Dragon Revolutionary Army
shot.fallback: hooded man in the rain with a long coat

lines.text: He is the leader of the Revolutionary Army, and the World Government treats him as its biggest threat.

shot.search: Dragon world's most wanted man bounty
shot.fallback: wanted poster of a tattooed man

lines.text: He's also Garp's son. Chapter 432 is where Garp casually tells Luffy that the revolutionary is his father.

shot.fallback: old marine telling a boy about his father

lines.text: Think about how strange that is. The Hero of the Marines raised a boy whose father is the Marines' greatest enemy.

shot.search: Garp Hero of the Marines Dragon Luffy
shot.fallback: old marine hero with a dog helmet beside a boy

lines.text: Dragon entrusted Luffy to Garp to be raised. That is a revolutionary leader choosing a hiding place.

shot.fallback: baby left with a marine at a mountain village

lines.text: I find that one of the smartest details in the story. You hide a revolutionary's son beside the man the Marines trust most.

shot.fallback: old marine hero beside a young boy

lines.text: It's the same instinct as Loguetown, and the same instinct as Mary Geoise. Hide the important piece inside the noise.

shot.fallback: hooded man watching a ship leave harbor

lines.text: And notice that Dragon has kept his distance from Luffy's rise, at least on the page.

shot.search: Dragon Luffy father watching Going Merry
shot.fallback: hooded father watching his son sail away

lines.text: He never reaches out to Luffy on the page. For a father, that is either cold or very disciplined.

shot.fallback: hooded man on a rooftop as a ship departs

lines.text: He pulled Luffy out of danger at Loguetown, and the world only saw a storm.

shot.fallback: strong wind hitting a marine captain

lines.text: I think Dragon treats the whole world the same way. He gives the pieces room, then lets the pressure do its work.

shot.fallback: hooded leader in a crowd of revolutionaries

lines.text: It's patient, and it also makes him hard to read, which might be why Oda keeps him off the page.

shot.fallback: shadowy leader with a hidden face

lines.text: There is a cost, though. A strategy this quiet means the Revolutionary Army can't save every ally in time.

shot.fallback: revolutionaries watching a distant island fire

lines.text: Kuma had to wait for a rescue. Lulusia was gone before the report even came in.

shot.fallback: freed man looking at a burning island

lines.text: Dragon's army is built on people who were lost, freed, and given a purpose. That is why they follow him so far.

shot.search: Revolutionary Army Sabo Koala Kuma freed
shot.fallback: freed slaves joining a revolutionary army

lines.text: That's the part of Dragon's character I find hardest to judge. His method works, and it also leaves people behind.

shot.fallback: leader looking at a map with crossed out islands

lines.text: Fans who love him tend to skip that. Fans who hate him tend to skip the results.

shot.fallback: two groups arguing in a tavern

lines.text: The truth is probably that Oda wants us uncomfortable with how much a good plan can cost.

shot.search: Eiichiro Oda One Piece Dragon morality
shot.fallback: long shadow of a leader over a ruined street

lines.text: I think the honest read sits in between. Dragon plays the long game, and he accepts what the long game costs.

shot.fallback: leader staring at a sunset on a cliff

lines.text: Which makes his next move the most important question in the series right now.

shot.fallback: leader walking toward a harbor at dawn

lines.text: If Imu has already paid for Elbaph with the Holy Land, what would Dragon do with an opening like that?

shot.search: Dragon Imu Elbaph Mary Geoise opening
shot.fallback: leader looking at an unguarded palace city

lines.text: Because there's one more detail that makes the timing look deliberate, and it's about who's still missing...

shot.search: Revolutionary Army Sabo Koala Karasu missing
shot.fallback: empty chairs in a revolutionary hideout

lines.text: Sabo, Karasu, Morley, Lindbergh, Koala, Ivankov. Where are they during all of this?

shot.search: Revolutionary Army Sabo Koala Ivankov Karasu
shot.fallback: six revolutionary commanders in a line

lines.text: In the Elbaph arc, we haven't seen the Revolutionary Army fight beside the Straw Hats at all.

shot.search: Elbaph arc Straw Hats Luffy Zoro Sanji
shot.fallback: straw hat crew in a giant forest

lines.text: That could mean they're busy. It could mean Oda is saving them for later. Or it could mean Dragon's plan is moving offscreen.

shot.fallback: shadowy revolutionaries on a distant ship

lines.text: I lean toward the third option, because everything the army has done so far happened offscreen first.

shot.fallback: flags rising behind a closed door

lines.text: Think about it as a mechanics question. Why show a revolution when you can show only its consequences, and let fans do the math?

shot.fallback: empty chair with a revolutionary coat

lines.text: The Eight-Nation Revolution is mostly reported in dialogue. Dragon's report is a conversation, and the raid itself arrives as a flashback.

shot.fallback: newspaper pages scattered on a table

lines.text: That structure is deliberate. We learn the outcome first, and the plan behind it is left for us to rebuild.

shot.search: Oda storytelling Revolutionary Army outcome plan
shot.fallback: puzzle pieces on a map table

lines.text: That is how Oda handles this organization. Results arrive first, and the explanation arrives much later.

shot.fallback: manga pages with revolutionary silhouettes

lines.text: It is the same trick with Kuma's past, and with Sabo's memory. Oda tells us the result and makes us earn the cause.

shot.fallback: two portraits of a tall man and a masked man

lines.text: And I think the Mary Geoise fire follows the same pattern. The explanation is coming. We just aren't there yet.

shot.fallback: palace city in smoke at dawn

lines.text: Here's the verdict, and I'll label it as a theory, because that's what it is.

shot.fallback: leader holding a lit candle over a map

lines.text: Dragon didn't plan Elbaph. He planned a world where Imu had to spend his Knights somewhere, and Mary Geoise couldn't cover itself.

shot.search: Dragon Imu Knights of God Mary Geoise
shot.fallback: empty palace with a hooded figure at the gate

lines.text: The raid created noise. The revolutions created pressure. And chapter 1083 shows he expected the Knights to be the answer.

shot.search: Dragon chapter 1083 Knights of God answer
shot.fallback: leader at a map table with a candle

lines.text: If that holds, then the Knights' absence from the Holy Land isn't luck. It's what a squeezed throne looks like.

shot.search: Knights of God absent Mary Geoise Holy Land
shot.fallback: empty throne beneath a high window

lines.text: It also gives us something to watch for: the next time Mary Geoise appears, count who is guarding it.

shot.search: Mary Geoise guards Holy Land count
shot.fallback: few guards standing at white gates

lines.text: If the Revolutionary Army shows up in Elbaph's aftermath, I'd bet it won't be to fight beside Luffy. It'll be to finish a job.

shot.fallback: masked revolutionaries arriving by sea at dawn

lines.text: Dragon taught the world one thing already. You don't have to win the loudest fight to change who wins the war.

shot.fallback: leader in a hood looking at a sunrise

lines.text: And if you want to see how Dragon first stepped into Luffy's story, that's the Loguetown video.

shot.fallback: hooded man in a storm watching a small ship
